info.title: MorphScreen API
info.summary: A model's answer as UI: validated, repaired and streamed, in our format.
info.description:
MorphScreen turns a model's answer into UI written in one format, checked by the core as it streams and repaired when it breaks a rule. Our own key goes in `X-MorphScreen-Key`. The model is included on paid plans (and 100 calls a month on the free one): leave out `Authorization` and the call runs deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash on our OpenRouter key (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash when that can't serve it; ask for either), reasoning off, at most about 8,000 tokens of conversation in and 4,000 out. To run any other model, send your own OpenRouter key as `Authorization: Bearer sk-or-...`; it's passed to OpenRouter and never kept.

Three ways in: `/v1/chat/completions` speaks OpenAI's and OpenRouter's chat format, so an app already on either switches by its base URL and one header; `/v1/ui` is an AG-UI run, what the MorphScreen SDKs read; `/v1/render` draws an answer you already have, with no model.

The options ride in one shape everywhere (`morphscreen` in a chat completion, `forwardedProps` in an AG-UI run, the body of a render): `packs`, `components`, `image_hosts`, `images`, `photos`, `output`, `repair`.

Errors come as `{"error": {"code": <HTTP status>, "message", "type": <our reason>, "metadata": {"error_type", "reason"}}}`, a shape both OpenAI's and OpenRouter's SDKs read; inside a stream, a failure is an `error` on a chunk, or an AG-UI `RUN_ERROR`.

openRouterKey.description: Your own OpenRouter key (`sk-or-...`), for any model: the model runs on it. Left out, the call runs the model included in your plan on ours. Passed to OpenRouter and nowhere else; never stored or logged.

morphscreenKey.name: X-MorphScreen-Key
morphscreenKey.description: Your MorphScreen key (ms_live_...): the call counts against your plan. Shown once when made; only its hash is kept.

dashboardSession.name: ms_session
dashboardSession.description: The session opening a sign-up or sign-in link, or signing in with GitHub, sets.

Options.description: How the answer is checked and what comes back.

packs.description: The core's packs to add: data, commerce, scheduling, media, docs, inputs, device, interactive, or all. Left out, every pack ("all"); [] for the core alone, a prompt about half as long.

components.description: Your own packs, in the shape the custom components docs give; 256 KB at most.

image_hosts.description: Hosts the HTML's pictures may load from, besides the app's images' hosts and its photo provider's.

images.description: Your own pictures, which the model shows by id.

output.description: What comes back; each endpoint has its own choices.

repair.description: Repair an answer with errors, and give a blank one a fresh try.

Message.description: A chat message, as OpenAI and OpenRouter take it.

ChatCompletionRequest.description: OpenAI's chat completion request. Every field not listed here (temperature, max_tokens, models, provider, reasoning...) goes to the model as you set it. DeepSeek V4 Flash answers with reasoning off unless you set `reasoning`.

model.description: An OpenRouter model name, like deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash.

morphscreen.description: output: text (the answer in our format, the default) or html (drawn by the core; not streamed).

Usage.description: Tokens and cost, OpenRouter's usage object as it came (its detail fields included).

class.description: What kind of problem: hallucinated-component, signature-mismatch, required-field, enum-mismatch, placement (content where its parent doesn't take it, like text directly inside a Quiz), malformed-syntax, unreadable-tag or unsafe-url. The op stream's `diag` op names the same field `cls`.

Repair.description: How a repair went. In a stream's last chunk it also carries the repaired `text` and whether it is `valid`.

nesting.description: Broken nesting mended with no model.

lines.description: The lines replaced, a number or [first, last].

Verdict.description: The core's word on the answer to draw: the repaired one when a repair kept one (its `repair.text` in a stream), else the answer as written. `repair.errors_before` counts what the written one had.

ChatCompletion.description: Through OpenRouter, the id, model (a fallback's, when one answered) and provider are OpenRouter's own.

RunAgentInput.description: AG-UI's RunAgentInput (protocol 1.0). Tools aren't supported yet: `tools` must be empty.

forwardedProps.description: The model and the options. output: agui (AG-UI events, the default) or ops (the core's op stream).

AguiEvent.description: An AG-UI event: RUN_STARTED, TEXT_MESSAGE_START, TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT, TEXT_MESSAGE_END, then MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT when a repair put its answer in place, CUSTOM morphscreen.verdict and morphscreen.repair, and RUN_FINISHED; or RUN_ERROR.

Op.description: One op of the core's op stream (the specification's Output section). After an `event: reset` a repaired answer's ops start again from the top; a failure is an `event: error` with {code, message}.

RenderRequest.description: An answer you already have, in our format, with the options. output: html (the default), ops or tree. Free, counted, within a fair-use limit.

images.description: Pictures the kept answer shows: their hosts are allowed in the HTML. The answer already has their addresses (img: ids were put in when it was made).

photos.description: Its provider's image hosts are allowed in the HTML; nothing is searched, as no model writes this answer.

RenderResponse.description: One of html, ops or tree, as output asked, with the verdict.

PromptRequest.description: The packs the answers may use (every pack when left out) and the app's own components.

code.description: The HTTP status (502, or 504 for a model that went quiet, inside a stream).

type.description: Our reason: invalid_json, model_required, model_not_found, openrouter_key_invalid, openrouter_out_of_credit, openrouter_rate_limited, payload_too_large, model_unavailable, model_error, model_timeout, and for sign-up: invalid_email, consent_required, bot_check_required, bot_check_failed, email_not_allowed, email_takes_no_mail, too_many_links, too_many_sign_ups, link_expired, sign_up_closed, mail_unavailable, and for billing: sign_in_required, already_subscribed, not_subscribed, billing_unavailable, billing_closed, invalid_signature

AppImage.description: One of your own pictures. The model shows it as ![alt](img:ID) and the API puts its URL and credit in; its host is allowed with it.

alt.description: What it shows, told to the model.

credit.description: Shown under it, as written (Markdown links allowed).

PhotoKey.description: The app's own photo key, for one provider: with it the model may ask for photos, searched there on the app's quota, each loading from the provider's own address with its credit. Without one (or with false) the model isn't asked for photos.

oneOf.description: The same as leaving it out.

app.description: Your app's name on Unsplash, for the credit's links.

email.description: The address to sign up with. Throwaway domains and domains that take no mail are turned down; Gmail's dots and any +tag are the same address.

consent.description: The version of the terms and privacy notice the person agreed to, like 2026-10-26.

turnstile.description: The token Cloudflare Turnstile gave the page.

device.description: FingerprintJS's visitor id. Kept only as a hash under our own pepper: a second free account from one device runs on its own OpenRouter key only.

from.description: Where the sign-up came from: ref and utm_* tags, kept with the sign-up; anything else is dropped.

consent.description: The version of the terms and privacy notice the person agreed to, like 2026-10-26.

turnstile.description: The token Cloudflare Turnstile gave the page.

device.description: FingerprintJS's visitor id. Kept only as a hash under our own pepper: a second free account from one device runs on its own OpenRouter key only.

from.description: Where the sign-up came from: ref and utm_* tags, kept with the sign-up; anything else is dropped.

turnstile.description: The token Cloudflare Turnstile gave the page.

sent.description: The same answer whether or not the address has an account.

token.description: The 64 characters after #t= in the link.

new.description: A new account; false for a sign-in.

key.description: A new account's first API key (ms_live_...), shown this once and never kept.

project.description: The project the key belongs to.

deleted.description: A deletion link: the account and everything it held are gone.

subscription.description: The subscription paying now, or the newest when none does: id, plan, yearly, currency, status (pending, active, on_hold, paused, cancelled, failed, expired, past_due), current_end (the next billing date), ends_at (set when it's cancelled to end with what's paid), next ({plan, yearly, starts_at}: a change set for the next billing date).

prices.description: Each paid plan's calls and, by currency, its price a month and a year in cents (USD) or paise (INR), tax included, and `extra`: an extra call past the month, in dollars or rupees.

tax_included.description: Every price includes its tax: Dodo Payments sells as the merchant of record and works out the tax in checkout.

portal.description: There's something paid, so /v1/billing/portal opens Dodo's page for invoices and the payment method.

test_mode.description: Billing runs against Dodo's test mode: no money moves.

given.description: The plan was given by us, not paid for: it stops at its month rather than running on as extra.

currency.description: Dollars unless rupees are picked; USD if left out.

included.description: Calls a month on our model; null: every call.

days.description: The last 30 days (UTC) with any use.

outcome.description: done, cut (at the model's length limit), failed, gone (the reader left), or the reason it was turned down.

path.description: The page's path, as location.pathname: lower-case letters, digits and / - _ .

source.description: Where the visit came from: the UTM source, or the referring host; empty for none.

Repairing.description: In a stream, after the answer's text: it had `errors` and a repair has started. The repaired answer, if one is kept, comes in the last chunk.

BadRequest.description: The request can't be run as written; model_needs_your_key: a model other than the included one, asked for without your own OpenRouter key.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or one turned down: your MorphScreen key (morphscreen_key_required, morphscreen_key_invalid) or your OpenRouter key (openrouter_key_required, openrouter_key_invalid).

PaymentRequired.description: This month's calls on your plan are used (plan_quota_reached), a paid plan's month and as many again as extra (extra_limit_reached), the free plan's calls with the model included (included_calls_used, or included_calls_paused while our credit is low), or the OpenRouter account is out of credit (openrouter_out_of_credit).

Forbidden.description: The account is suspended (account_suspended), or the model's moderation refused the request (model_refused).

TooLarge.description: The body is over 1 MB (payload_too_large), or a call with the model included has more than about 8,000 tokens of conversation (conversation_too_long).

TooMany.description: A limit reached, with Retry-After saying how long to wait: requests a minute (rate_limited), answers at once (too_many_streams), the free tier's day (daily_limit_reached), renders this month (render_limit_reached), or OpenRouter's own (openrouter_rate_limited).

BadGateway.description: The model failed or couldn't be reached, after the retries.

GatewayTimeout.description: The model took too long to start.

Unavailable.description: Accounts can't be read just now; try again.

Gone.description: link_expired: the link was used, has expired, or was never ours. Ask for a new one.

Conflict.description: already_subscribed: the account already pays for a plan (change it instead); not_subscribed: there's no plan to change, cancel or open the portal for; same_plan: it's on that plan already; yearly_stays_yearly: a yearly plan changes only to another yearly one; ending: the plan is set to end (keep it first); already_cancelled: it's set to end already; not_cancelled: there's no cancel to take back.

post.summary: A chat completion in our format, OpenAI's and OpenRouter's request and response

200.description: The answer whole, or with stream true as server-sent events: chat.completion.chunk after chunk, the last with finish_reason and morphscreen (and the repaired text when a repair was needed), a usage chunk when asked, then `data: [DONE]`.

post.summary: An AG-UI run (protocol 1.0), what the MorphScreen SDKs read

200.description: Server-sent events: AG-UI events (output agui), or the core's ops (output ops).

post.summary: An answer you already have, drawn again with no model

200.description: The answer as HTML, ops or the tree, with the core's verdict.

400.description: The request can't be run as written: invalid_json, invalid_input, invalid_options or invalid_catalog, or text_required: no `text`.

429.description: A limit reached, with Retry-After saying how long to wait: requests a minute (rate_limited), or renders this month (render_limit_reached).

post.summary: The system prompt for some packs, for an agent that runs its own model
post.description: The same text the web SDK's core.prompt(packs) gives. Not counted.

400.description: The request can't be run as written: invalid_json, invalid_input, invalid_options or invalid_catalog.

429.description: A limit reached, with Retry-After saying how long to wait: requests a minute (rate_limited).

post.summary: Counts a page seen on the website, without cookies
post.description: What morphscreen.com sends as a page loads. The visitor is told apart for the day by a hash of their address and user agent under a secret made each day and never stored; a page counts once per visitor a day. Bots, malformed paths and repeats are answered the same way and not counted.

204.description: Counted, or not counted: the answer is the same.

post.summary: A magic link to sign up, or to sign in when the address has an account
post.description: At most 3 links an hour to one address and 10 sign-ups a day from one network. The mail goes to the address; nothing in the answer says whether it has an account.

202.description: The link is on its way.

post.summary: Opens a magic link: a new account with its first key, a sign-in, or a deletion
post.description: A sign-up or a sign-in also sets the ms_session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 30 days). A link works once, for 15 minutes.

post.summary: GitHub's page to sign up or in on
post.description: Takes what a sign-up by mail takes, less the address: GitHub's verified primary address is used. Sets a short-lived state cookie the way back checks; open `url` in the same browser. The account is the one linked to that GitHub account, else the one at its address (linked from then on), else a new one under sign-up's rules.

get.summary: Back from GitHub: a session, then the dashboard
get.description: GitHub sends the browser here. It answers with a redirect (303): to the dashboard's /welcome for a new account, its home otherwise, setting the session; or to /signin?error=<reason> (github_cancelled, github_failed, github_expired, github_email_unverified, github_other_account, email_not_allowed, too_many_sign_ups, accounts_unavailable, github_closed).

303.description: To the dashboard, or back to its sign-in page with the reason.

post.summary: A link that deletes an account and everything it holds
post.description: Opening the link (POST /v1/signup/verify) deletes the account, its projects, keys, usage and records. The mail goes to the address; nothing in the answer says whether it has an account.

202.description: The link is on its way, when the address has an account.

get.summary: The dashboard's account: its plan's limits, usage by day, projects and keys
The account's newest calls (100), never a prompt or an answer

parameters.name: failed
parameters.description: true: only calls that failed or whose answer wasn't valid.

post.summary: A new key for a project, shown this once
post.description: At most 20 live keys a project. Only the key's hash is kept.

project.description: The project's name (app, the first one, when left out).

post.summary: The account's key with this prefix stops working in 8 seconds

prefix.description: The key's first 12 characters, as the account lists them.

200.description: Revoked; the key stops working at stops_at.

stops_at.description: When calls with the key start being turned away.

post.description: The key keeps working for 8 seconds, so the revoke can be undone with /v1/account/keys/restore; then every call with it is turned away.

post.summary: A revoke taken back while the key still works

prefix.description: The key's first 12 characters, as the account lists them.

200.description: Restored: the key works as before.

409.description: Too late: the key has already stopped working (`too_late`).

post.description: Within 8 seconds of a revoke the key keeps working, and this takes the revoke back. After that it has stopped for good.

post.summary: Keeps a project's prompts and answers 7 days, to debug, or stops
Ends this session

get.summary: The account's plan, its subscription and the prices

post.summary: A subscription to Build or Scale, paid in Dodo Payments' checkout
post.description: Open `url` (Dodo's checkout, as an overlay over the dashboard or a page of its own). Once paid, checkout returns to the dashboard's billing page with `subscription_id` and `status`, which go to /v1/billing/confirm. A second request for the same plan within a day gets the same checkout.

post.summary: Back from checkout: the subscription Dodo made, applied at once
post.description: With `subscription` (the id checkout returned with) or without it (from the checkout over the dashboard): then the account's own checkouts, newest first, are looked up with Dodo. Dodo is asked where the subscription stands; when it's this account's, that's applied, so the plan starts now rather than with the webhook (which still comes, and changes nothing twice). Nothing paid yet answers `pending`.

200.description: Where the subscription stands, and the account's plan now.

status.description: Dodo's status for the subscription: active once the first payment went through, pending while it's still on its way.

post.summary: Another plan on the same subscription: now, or from the next billing date

200.description: Changed now, or set to change at the next billing date.

starts_at.description: When a change set for the next billing date starts.

subscription.description: The subscription as it is now, as GET /v1/billing gives it.

post.description: A higher plan takes effect at once, the difference for the rest of the period charged now and the billing date kept; monthly to yearly takes effect at once, a year starting today less what's left of the month. A lower plan starts at the next billing date, nothing charged now; choosing the plan it's on before then takes that back (`kept`). A change now waits on its charge: `charging` means Dodo hasn't taken it yet, and the plan moves when it does. Yearly to monthly isn't offered (409 yearly_stays_yearly); a plan set to end is kept first (409 ending).

post.summary: Cancels the plan at the end of what's paid; then the free plan
post.description: A change set for the next billing date goes with it. The plan can be kept until then with /v1/billing/keep.

post.summary: A cancel taken back: the plan renews as before
post.description: Nothing is charged now; the subscription renews at its next billing date.

post.summary: Dodo's page for the account's invoices and payment method

200.description: A link to Dodo's customer portal, good for a short while.

post.summary: Dodo Payments' webhooks
post.description: Standard Webhooks: webhook-signature is HMAC-SHA256 of `webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.body` with the webhook secret, the timestamp within five minutes; each is handled once by webhook-id. Subscription events are applied in the order they happened (the payload's `timestamp`), not the order they came in.
